nodes.label: graphify project rules (CLAUDE.md)
nodes.rationale: Querying the graph returns a scoped subgraph that is usually far smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output, so codebase questions should hit graphify query first; graphify update . is AST-only so it costs no API tokens.

nodes.label: Fast path for an existing graph
nodes.source_location: What You Must Do When Invoked
nodes.rationale: If graphify-out/graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language codebase question, Steps 1-5 are skipped entirely and graphify query runs immediately - rebuilding a graph that is already built wastes tokens and time.
nodes.norm_label: fast path for an existing graph

nodes.label: Structural (AST) extraction - Part A
nodes.rationale: Code is extracted deterministically with no LLM and no API key at all, so a code-only corpus skips semantic extraction entirely and costs nothing.

nodes.label: Semantic extraction via parallel subagents - Part B
nodes.rationale: Subagents must be dispatched in ONE message so they run in parallel, and must be general-purpose (Explore is read-only and silently drops chunk files). Reading files one-by-one is 5-10x slower.
nodes.norm_label: semantic extraction via parallel subagents - part b

nodes.label: Semantic extraction cache (prompt-attributed)
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are stamped with the extraction prompt (SPEC_PATH) that produced them so an upgraded prompt re-extracts instead of replaying stale results (#1939).

nodes.label: No API key required policy
nodes.rationale: graphify never reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY; Gemini is used only when GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY happens to be set, otherwise the host agent itself is the LLM. Prompting for a key is a misread of the skill.

nodes.label: Graph health check (integrity gate)
nodes.rationale: Read-only and never aborts: it surfaces edge collapse, dangling/missing endpoints and self-loops - the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches - without blocking a usable graph.

nodes.label: graph.json shrink guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to write when the new graph is smaller than the existing graph.json, and GRAPH_REPORT.md plus the analysis sidecar are only written after a successful write, so they never describe a graph graph.json does not contain (#1392).

nodes.label: Extraction manifest and stamping
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped; a detected file whose chunk failed must stay unstamped so the next --update re-queues it, otherwise its content is lost forever (#2015).

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS), never skip the corpus warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion behind symbols, never run HTML viz above 5000 nodes without warning - the audit trail is the product.

nodes.label: Node ID format rule
nodes.rationale: IDs must be the full repo-relative path stem plus the entity so they match what the AST extractor generates; filename-only or immediate-parent-only IDs create orphan ghost-duplicate nodes, and any chunk suffix breaks determinism.

nodes.label: Confidence score rubric
nodes.rationale: Discrete values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) are used instead of a continuous range because production showed models collapsing the range to a bimodal binary (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+).

nodes.label: source_file verbatim rule
nodes.rationale: Copying the FILE_LIST path character-for-character keeps the full build and incremental --update on the same base so build_merge's replace-on-re-extract matches the existing node instead of accumulating duplicates.

nodes.label: Constrained query expansion
nodes.rationale: The query CLI matches by case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming, synonyms or cross-language matching, so a wording mismatch returns 0 hits; the question is expanded only against tokens that actually exist in the graph vocabulary, never invented ones.

nodes.label: BFS / DFS traversal modes
nodes.rationale: BFS answers 'what is X connected to' (broad, nearest neighbors first); DFS answers 'how does X reach Y' (traces a chain, depth-limited to 6).

nodes.label: save-result feedback loop
nodes.rationale: Saving the answer (with the expanded-token trace) back into the graph means the next --update extracts the Q&A as a node, closing the feedback loop so future queries improve.

nodes.label: Work memory / LESSONS.md reflection
nodes.rationale: Outcomes (useful / dead_end / corrected) accumulate into preferred sources, known dead ends and corrections; graphify reflect --if-stale is deterministic and free so a session-start run costs almost nothing.

nodes.label: Incremental --update flow
nodes.rationale: Code-only changes skip semantic extraction entirely (no LLM); files carries only the changed subset while all_files carries the full corpus so later steps still have corpus-wide context.

nodes.label: build_merge (replace-on-re-extract)
nodes.rationale: build_merge reads graph.json directly without a NetworkX round-trip so edge direction is preserved (#801); prune_sources is only for genuinely deleted files because changed files are reconciled by replace-on-re-extract (#1344), and root= is required or nothing is pruned and stale nodes accumulate (#1361).

nodes.label: --cluster-only
nodes.rationale: graphify cluster-only . is self-contained; re-running Steps 5-9 afterwards raises FileNotFoundError because Step 9 cleanup already deleted the intermediate files (#1392).

nodes.label: Whisper video/audio transcription
nodes.rationale: The host agent writes the Whisper initial prompt itself from god-node labels - it is already a language model, so no separate API call is needed; transcript JSON is written from Python rather than a shell redirect because Whisper progress on stdout would corrupt the file (#1392).

nodes.label: --watch auto-rebuild
nodes.rationale: Code-only changes rebuild immediately with no LLM; doc/paper/image changes only raise a needs_update flag because they require paid semantic re-extraction. Debounce exists so a wave of parallel agent writes does not trigger one rebuild per file.

nodes.label: post-commit auto-rebuild hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit instead of holding a background process, works with any editor, and appends to an existing post-commit hook rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: FalkorDB export
nodes.rationale: The generated file is OpenCypher, but FalkorDB's GRAPH.QUERY runs one statement at a time with no bulk script import, so --falkordb-push is preferred over the portable cypher.txt artifact.

nodes.label: MCP stdio server (graphify.serve)
nodes.rationale: Claude Desktop cannot run $(...) and under uv tool install the system python3 cannot import graphify, so the config must use the absolute interpreter path from .graphify_python.

nodes.label: Token reduction benchmark
nodes.rationale: Skipped silently below 5000 words because for small corpora the value of the graph is structural clarity, not token compression.

nodes.label: merge-graphs (cross-repo / monorepo)
nodes.rationale: The skill pipeline always writes to graphify-out/ in the cwd, so running it per subfolder would clobber the same output dir; the CLI is used instead because it places graphify-out/ inside each scanned path, then the graphs are merged at the root.

nodes.label: Deploy docs to GitHub Pages workflow
nodes.norm_label: deploy docs to github pages workflow

nodes.label: WebGPU first / WebGL 2 fallback
nodes.rationale: Shaders are written as TSL node factories rather than GLSL strings so three can transpile to WGSL or GLSL automatically - the consumer writes one implementation for both backends. WebGPU device acquisition is async, hence the ready Promise.

nodes.label: Scroll sync (effective scrollY)
nodes.rationale: Effective scrollY comes from -document.documentElement.getBoundingClientRect().top rather than window.scrollY so that iOS Safari rubber-band / pull-to-refresh offsets are captured; feeding the same value to both the container transform and the plane positions keeps canvas and DOM visually aligned without killing pull-to-refresh.

nodes.label: Single rAF loop (Lenis integration)
nodes.rationale: Two separate rAF loops run in registration order, so if Core registers first it reads a one-frame-stale scrollY and the background canvas drifts while scrolling. Driving lenis.raf() then app.tick() from one loop guarantees ordering. The old rafScroll option / RafScroll class / getRafScroll() were removed as part of this.

nodes.label: Peer dependency / bundle policy
nodes.rationale: three (>= 0.178.0), lil-gui and stats.js are peer dependencies and Lenis is not a runtime dependency at all - smooth scrolling is treated as an app concern; sideEffects: false keeps tree-shaking working.

nodes.label: ready (async init Promise)
nodes.rationale: Awaiting is optional: before init completes render() is a no-op while createPlane()/update() are safe because update() never touches the GPU. It rejects only when neither WebGPU nor WebGL 2 is available.

nodes.label: isWebGPUBackend()
nodes.rationale: Returns false before ready resolves because the backend is only decided after async init - callers must await ready before branching on it.

nodes.label: tick(time?)
nodes.rationale: A thin facade over update() then render(); time is accepted only for API symmetry with Lenis since elapsed time actually comes from an internal THREE.Clock.

nodes.label: update(time?) / render(options?)
nodes.rationale: Splitting state update from draw lets render() save and restore whatever RenderTarget was bound before the call and write only to outputTarget, so multiple scenes can be drawn into external FBOs for transitions without corrupting them.

nodes.label: setPostEffect(effectLike, options?)
nodes.rationale: Ownership defaults to domSyncGL (it disposes the previous postEffect on replace/clearEffects/destroy); { owned: false } hands dispose back to the caller. Mixing it with addEffect() destroys the internal EffectComposer, so it throws in DEV.

nodes.label: effectSamples (MSAA)
nodes.rationale: MSAA on the scene RenderTarget prevents jagged edges once effects are enabled; clamped to the GPU limit or the WebGPU standard 4 when the limit cannot be read.

nodes.label: stats.js / lil-gui instance injection
nodes.rationale: showStats / showGUI / statsParent / guiTitle were removed: creation, DOM insertion and disposal are the caller's responsibility so the library merely uses the instance handed to it, and dev tools can be dynamic-imported out of the production bundle.

nodes.label: enableOrbitControls()
nodes.rationale: Under scrollSync the container has pointer-events: none, so orbit controls re-enable pointer events on the canvas only.

nodes.label: PlaneNodeContext (built-in nodes)
nodes.rationale: The node graph is built once at plane construction; per-frame updates only swap .value on the context nodes. Built-in names are reserved uniforms and passing a same-named node via options.uniforms throws because the library updates them every frame.

nodes.label: DomPlane.addFeedback (generator)
nodes.rationale: addEffect is a sink that post-processes the picture while addFeedback is a generator that produces a source texture - the output direction is reversed. Because the colorNode graph is fixed at construction, the destination texture() node must be pre-declared in options.uniforms under the same name as outputUniform or it throws.

nodes.label: textureColorSpace default (SRGBColorSpace)
nodes.rationale: Changed from the v0.3 NoColorSpace default because NodeMaterial performs the color-space conversion at screen output: decoding to linear on sample and re-encoding to sRGB on output makes the plane match the DOM . NoColorSpace is now only for raw data textures.

nodes.label: getComputedStyle rasterization pipeline
nodes.rationale: Styles are always read from getComputedStyle so fluid values like font-size: clamp(...) resolve on their own and breakpoints never have to be duplicated in JS - the way to change the plane's look is to edit CSS, not JS.

nodes.label: color: transparent text hiding
nodes.source_location: なぜ display: none にしないのか
nodes.rationale: visibility / display / opacity are deliberately avoided: making the text transparent keeps layout, accessibility (screen readers), SEO and text selection intact in the DOM while only the visual layer moves to WebGL.

nodes.label: Text layout rules (paragraphs, wrapping, 4096px clamp)
nodes.rationale: Canvas side length is clamped at 4096px so a huge element on a high-DPR screen cannot blow out VRAM. Because textContent is used verbatim, HTML indentation newlines also become paragraph breaks - write the text on one line or pass the text option.

nodes.label: document.fonts.ready wait before first rasterize
nodes.source_location: フォントの読み込み待ち
nodes.rationale: The first rasterization waits on document.fonts.ready so text is not baked with the pre-webfont fallback face; if fonts are already loaded it draws immediately.

nodes.label: loadFont()
nodes.rationale: Never rejects on failure - it warns and resolves so callers do not need a catch everywhere and CSS fallbacks simply take over. Failed fonts are dropped from the cache so a transient network error can be retried, successful ones are never re-fetched.

nodes.label: Font loading separated from DomTextPlane
nodes.source_location: DomTextPlane とは分離されている
nodes.rationale: Fetching and registering fonts is not DomTextPlane's responsibility; loadFont only adds to document.fonts while createTextPlane keeps reading getComputedStyle, which is what lets CSS (including clamp() fluid values) stay the single source of truth for font-size/weight.

nodes.label: getConfig(): BaseEffectConfig
nodes.rationale: outputNode is invoked exactly once when the pass is registered; every later frame updates only the .value of the UniformNodes passed in uniforms (setUniform), so the node graph is never rebuilt.

nodes.label: Built-in runtime state (uTime / uMouse / width / height)
nodes.source_location: 組み込みの実行時状態
nodes.rationale: The owner updates these through an internal API immediately before update()/resize(), so subclasses cannot break them by forgetting super.update()/super.resize().
nodes.norm_label: built-in runtime state (utime / umouse / width / height)

nodes.label: No resolution uniform (use TSL screenSize)
nodes.source_location: 解像度 uniform は用意していない
nodes.rationale: screenSize auto-updates every render with no dummy value or wiring, but it reports the currently bound RenderTarget's size; width/height exist only for the JS-side real numbers TSL cannot supply, e.g. new THREE.RenderTarget(w, h).

nodes.label: BaseEffect feedback buffer
nodes.source_location: フィードバックバッファ
nodes.rationale: BaseEffect owns the ping-pong RenderTarget pair, first clear, per-frame draw and swap, resize and disposal so a subclass only writes the accumulation formula. The buffer lives off-screen and is not automatically in the post chain, so nothing appears until outputNode composites feedbackTexture with inputTexture.

nodes.label: HalfFloat default for feedback buffers
nodes.source_location: 既定が HalfFloat な理由
nodes.rationale: At 8-bit, 10/255 multiplied by 0.95 rounds back to 10/255, so a decaying trail never fades and leaves a ghost; repeated-decay effects need HalfFloat or better.

nodes.label: feedback.node evaluation timing
nodes.rationale: The accumulation buffer is drawn before the composer's render() (right after update()), so inputTexture at that moment points at last frame's about-to-be-overwritten ping-pong target and is meaningless; mixing in the previous pass must happen in outputNode instead. Uniforms changed inside update() are reflected immediately.

nodes.label: RafScroll (removed)
nodes.rationale: The Lenis wrapper was deleted on the principle that smooth scrolling is an application concern, not something the library should own; the rafScroll option and getRafScroll() went with it.

nodes.label: overscan
nodes.rationale: Extends canvas height to viewportHeight + 2*overscan so a mobile URL-bar resize cannot expose a clipped canvas edge. 'auto' only pays that cost under (pointer: coarse) - 0 on mouse environments - so the default protects touch devices without wasting desktop pixels. Falls back to 0 where window.matchMedia is missing (SSR).

nodes.label: attach ('translate' | 'dom')
nodes.rationale: 'dom' respects the container's own CSS placement and never overwrites position/size/transform, but a non-fixed container scrolls with the page so canvasRect goes stale and DomPlane can drift; overscan does not apply.

nodes.label: ScrollSync.computeEffectiveScrollY()
nodes.rationale: Returns -document.documentElement.getBoundingClientRect().top, which equals window.scrollY normally but goes negative during an iOS Safari top rubber-band because it folds in the visual viewport offset.

nodes.label: strength / trackStrength
nodes.rationale: Tracking is opt-in: reading strength with trackStrength: false always returns 0 and DEV warns once, so the cost is not paid unless the effect actually needs scroll velocity.
